title: Correlation of infectious diseases and clonal hematopoiesis
summary:
With increasing age, a majority of the population carries a hidden, asymptomatic infectious disease. Simultaneously, the number of individuals with genetic alterations in their blood-forming stem cells also increases with age. It is known that inflammatory processes can negatively impact blood cell production.
This project therefore aims to investigate whether there is a correlation between the presence of hidden, asymptomatic infections and the frequency of genetic alterations in blood-forming stem cells.
This will be investigated by analyzing surplus blood material collected during voluntary blood donations from healthy donors for corresponding genetic alterations and previous infections.

interventions.name: Excess material from healthy blood donors is examined for the presence of infectious diseases and clonal hematopoiesis.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Apart from the age requirement of 40 and over, the same inclusion criteria apply as for a regular, voluntary blood donation. Furthermore, consent to "research on surplus material" (as part of the regular "donor questionnaire") is required. Once this consent has been given, agreement to the study-specific "information sheet and informed consent form" must also be provided.
Exclusion criteria:
Age under 40 years and the exclusion criteria for regular, voluntary blood donation. Lack of consent to "research on surplus material" or to the study-specific "information sheet and consent form".
